    Power calculation for Single-test Diagnostic Accuracy Study with Co-Primary Endpoints

    power_opt_bin.Rd

    The function determines the achieved overall power for a confirmatory diagnostic accuracy study with co-primary endpoints (sensitivity and specificity) for a fixed total sample size.

    Both endpoints are tested for superiority against fixed null values. Study success requires rejection of both null hypotheses. Overall power is therefore defined under an intersection–union testing (IUT) framework, meaning that both tests must be significant. Under this framework, the global Type I error rate is controlled at level \(\alpha\) without multiplicity adjustment.

    The calculation explicitly incorporates the assumed disease prevalence, which determines the expected number of diseased and non-diseased subjects.

    power_opt_bin(
  N,
  prev,
  se.e,
  se.min,
  sp.e,
  sp.min,
  alpha = 0.025,
  ci_method = c("wald", "logit"),
  alternative = c("one.sided", "two.sided")
)

    Arguments

    N

    Total sample size.

    prev

    Disease prevalence (0 < prev < 1).

    se.e

    Sensitivity under the alternative hypothesis.

    se.min

    Sensitivity under the null hypothesis.

    sp.e

    Specificity under the alternative hypothesis.

    sp.min

    Specificity under the null hypothesis.

    alpha

    Type I error level.

    ci_method

    Normal approximation method: "wald" (default) or "logit".

    alternative

    "one.sided" (default) or "two.sided".

    Value

    An object of class `"dx_bin"` containing:

    • design specifications (design specifications (alpha level, testing framework, CI method)

    • achieved overall power,

    • endpoint-specific powers,

    • subgroup sample sizes.

    Details

    Let \(\pi\) denote the assumed disease prevalence. The study population is partitioned into diseased (\(N_{Se} = N\pi\)) and non-diseased (\(N_{Sp} = N(1-\pi)\)) independent subgroups.

    Endpoint-specific powers are derived from the asymptotic normal test statistics corresponding to the sample size formulas. The implementation uses large-sample approximations for binomial proportions based on either:

    • the Wald approximation on the probability scale, or

    • the logit-transformed normal approximation.

    Under standard binomial sampling assumptions, the estimators of sensitivity and specificity are asymptotically independent.

    Overall power is therefore computed as:

    $$ Power_{overall} = Power_{Se} \times Power_{Sp}. $$

    The function returns the achieved endpoint-specific powers and their joint probability for the specified total sample size.

    References

    Stark, M., & Zapf, A. (2020). Sample size calculation and re-estimation based on the prevalence in a single-arm confirmatory diagnostic accuracy study. *Statistical Methods in Medical Research*, 29(10), 2958–2971. doi:10.1177/0962280220913588 The power calculation implemented in this function is consistent with the asymptotic normal framework underlying the sample size methodology described in the above reference.

    See also

    ss_opt_bin

    Author

    Maia Muresan (DCR Bern)

    Examples

    
# Example 1: Achieved power for a fixed sample size
# Objective: evaluate power to demonstrate that sensitivity
# and specificity exceed pre-specified minimum values
power_opt_bin(
  N = 122,            # total sample size
  prev = 0.5,         # disease prevalence
  se.e = 0.85,        # expected sensitivity
  se.min = 0.65,      # minimum acceptable sensitivity
  sp.e = 0.85,        # expected specificity
  sp.min = 0.55,      # minimum acceptable specificity
  alpha = 0.025       # one-sided significance level
)
#> 
#> DxPower - Confirmatory Diagnostic Accuracy Study 
#> --------------------------------------------------
#> Design:            single-test design 
#> Framework:        Co-primary (IUT)
#> Alpha level:       0.025 (one.sided) 
#> Prevalence:        0.5 
#> 
#> Hypotheses:
#>   Sensitivity :    sup 
#>   Specificity :    sup 
#> 
#> Achieved overall power:  0.96 
#> 
#> Endpoint-specific power:
#>   Sensitivity:      0.961 
#>   Specificity:      1 
#> 
#> Sample size per group:
#>   Total:            122 
#>   Diseased:         61 
#>   Non-diseased:     61 
#> 
#same
power_opt_bin(
  N = 122,            # total sample size
  prev = 0.5,         # disease prevalence
  se.e = 0.85,        # expected sensitivity
  se.min = 0.65,      # minimum acceptable sensitivity
  sp.e = 0.85,        # expected specificity
  sp.min = 0.55,      # minimum acceptable specificity
  alpha = 0.025,      # one-sided significance level (default)
  ci_method = "wald"  # default

)

#> DxPower - Confirmatory Diagnostic Accuracy Study

  N = 122,
  prev = 0.5,
